endorsements.quote: Health care providers are ethically and legally obliged to obtain informed consent when providing a health intervention [ 101 , 102 ].
The identification of algorithmic bias requires proactive and prospective performance monitoring.
Where such discrepancies are identified, more detailed information could be collected for this segment to enable retraining of the model to improve both fairness and accuracy [ 125 ].

Similarly, when an algorithm triggers the necessity for clinical contact, the clinician should be provided with guidance on how to interpret the thresholds for action through transparency on the difference between the person’s demographics compared with the algorithmic training cohort [ 125 ].
The ongoing engagement and consent of people who use drugs, multiple disadvantaged groups, and their advocates is critical to ensuring the impact of data absenteeism is managed and attenuated.

unlisted_practices: Establish a mandated system for monitoring and reporting errors arising from big data and AI analytics tools in health care settings.
Strengthen regulation of Software as a Medical Device products used in clinical care.
Define lines of accountability for AI error detection, whether the manufacturer's or an independent regulator's responsibility.
Design AI and big data interfaces to be unobtrusive and to facilitate person-centered care.
Strengthen existing health care infrastructure so services can respond to increased demand generated by AI predictive and diagnostic outputs.
Protect people seeking OUD treatment from being disadvantaged if they decline consent to big data initiatives or withdraw their data.
Enact robust data protection laws so patients are reassured that sensitive data will not be exploited or repurposed to their detriment.
Use trusted research environments to control access to individual-level data and prevent re-identification.
Raise awareness of data security breach risks and mitigation measures when obtaining informed consent for AI data use.
Provide patients a reasonable alternative should they refuse consent to AI or big data use.
Select data types and streams for AI models based on existing evidence and clinical expertise rather than adding data simply because they are available.
Involve affected communities in identifying research questions for big data initiatives.
